title: How long does metal last?
tagline: Rust, dust and a million years
dadNotes: Apollo 11's lander base is still on the Moon, more than 50 years on, with no rust.
Rust needs water and air. The Moon has neither, so its metal stays shiny.
Venus is about 465 degrees Celsius. The Venera 13 probe lasted 127 minutes, about as long as a film.
Opportunity was built for 90 Mars days and worked for nearly 15 years.
Voyager 1 has been flying since 1977 and still sends messages home.
Starship is made of stainless steel: cheap, tough in the cold, and better at handling heat than carbon fibre (Elon Musk's reasons).

steps.title: Still there after 50 years
steps.text: This photo was taken from space, of the place where Apollo 11 landed on the Moon. The lander's base is still there, more than fifty years later.
steps.dad: Ask Finn: why do you think it has not rusted?

steps.title: Guess!
steps.prompt: Where would a steel bike last the longest?
steps.reveal: Good guess! On the Moon there is no air and no water, so there is no rust. A beach has both air and water, so rust grows there. Venus is very hot and has acid in its clouds, so it is the hardest place of all.

steps.title: The Metal Time Machine
steps.intro: Pick a place and an object, then drag the time slider to see what happens to it.

steps.title: Rust by the sea
steps.text: On Earth, rust needs water and air to grow. A beach has both, so iron and steel go brown and crumbly.
steps.wow: Rust can slowly eat through steel!
steps.dad: Ask Finn: have you ever seen something go rusty?

steps.title: Hot Venus
steps.text: Venus is about 465 degrees Celsius, much hotter than any oven at home. In 1982 a Soviet probe landed there, and it sent back this picture of the ground.
steps.wow: It lasted 127 minutes, about as long as a film!

steps.title: Built for three months
steps.text: A rover called Opportunity was built to work on Mars for just 90 Mars days, about three months. It kept going for much longer.

steps.title: Still flying
steps.text: Voyager 1 is a spacecraft that has been flying since 1977. It is now the furthest spacecraft from Earth, and it still sends messages home.
steps.dad: Ask Finn: what would you want to tell someone who finds Voyager?

steps.title: Try it at home: The three rusty nails
need: three clean jam jars with lids
steps: Jar 1: put a nail in, add water and a spoon of salt, then put the lid on.
Jar 2: put a nail in with nothing else, then put the lid on. This one stays dry.
Jar 3: put a nail in, add water, then pour a thin layer of oil on top. Put the lid on.
Check the nails tomorrow, and again in a week. Which one went rusty first?
Ask Finn: what do you think would happen to all three nails on the Moon?
steps.why: Rust needs water and air. The oil keeps air away from jar 3, and on the Moon all three nails would stay shiny.

debrief: Why do you think SpaceX chose steel for Starship?
